questions.question: A 54-year-old male with chronic hypertension is prescribed an ACE inhibitor. He develops an intractable dry cough and angioedema. This adverse effect is mediated by the accumulation of which substance, and what is its physiological action on blood pressure?
options: Bradykinin; causes systemic vasodilation and increased vascular permeability
questions.explanation: ACE (Kininase II) degrades bradykinin. Inactivation of ACE leads to bradykinin and substance P accumulation in the lungs, triggering bronchoconstriction, cough, and angioedema while contributing to peripheral vasodilation.
subject: Pharmacology
General Medicine

questions.question: Which of the following structures passes through the foramen magnum within the subarachnoid space?
options: Vertebral arteries and spinal accessory nerve roots
questions.explanation: The vertebral arteries, anterior/posterior spinal arteries, and spinal accessory nerve roots enter the posterior cranial fossa through the foramen magnum within the subarachnoid space.
subject: Anatomy

questions.question: A 4-day-old infant develops lethargy, vomiting, and metabolic acidosis with ketonuria. Lab tests show elevated leucine, isoleucine, and valine. The deficient enzyme complex in this condition normally requires which cofactor?
questions.explanation: Maple Syrup Urine Disease (MSUD) results from deficient branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex, which requires TLCFN cofactors: Thiamine (B1), Lipoate, CoA, FAD, and NAD+.
subject: Biochemistry
Pediatrics

questions.question: What is the primary electrocardiographic hallmark of acute hyperkalemia before the development of sine waves?
options: Tall, peaked, narrow-based T waves with shortened QT interval
Prominent U waves with ST depression
Delta waves with widened QRS complex
questions.explanation: Early hyperkalemia accelerates phase 3 repolarization of myocardial action potentials, manifesting on ECG as symmetrical, tall, tented/peaked T waves.
subject: General Medicine
Physiology

questions.question: A 28-year-old female presents with malar rash, photosensitivity, arthralgias, and hematuria. Renal biopsy demonstrates diffuse proliferative glomerulonephritis (Class IV Lupus Nephritis). Which antibody titer strongly correlates with active renal disease?
questions.explanation: Anti-dsDNA levels fluctuate with SLE disease activity and directly correlate with immune-complex mediated glomerulonephritis (lupus nephritis flares).
subject: Pathology
General Medicine

questions.question: A victim found dead in a closed room during a fire exhibits cherry-red postmortem lividity. Autopsy reveals carbon soot in the mainstem bronchi. What is the lethal mechanism of the primary toxic agent?
options: Competitive inhibition of oxygen binding to hemoglobin and leftward shift of dissociation curve
Irreversible inhibition of cytochrome c oxidase
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide binds hemoglobin with >200x affinity compared to O2, forming carboxyhemoglobin (cherry-red lividity) and shifting the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve to the left.
subject: Forensic Medicine
Pathology

questions.question: According to the WHO SAFE strategy for trachoma elimination, the antibiotic component primarily utilizes mass administration of:
questions.explanation: The 'A' in the WHO SAFE strategy stands for Antibiotics, using single-dose oral Azithromycin for community-wide mass drug administration against Chlamydia trachomatis.
subject: Ophthalmology
PSM / Community Med

questions.question: A 32-year-old male with a high-speed motorcycle collision presents with severe right leg pain out of proportion to exam findings, passive stretch pain, and tense swelling following a proximal tibial fracture. What is the immediate definitive management?
options: Closed reduction and long-leg plaster slab application
CT angiography of the lower limb
questions.explanation: Acute compartment syndrome is a surgical emergency diagnosed clinically by severe pain out of proportion and pain on passive stretch. Immediate four-compartment decompression fasciotomy prevents tissue necrosis.
subject: Orthopedics
General Surgery

questions.question: A 35-year-old pregnant female at 34 weeks of gestation presents with painless, recurrent, bright red vaginal bleeding. Her uterus is soft and non-tender. Fetal heart sounds are normal. What diagnostic examination is strictly contraindicated?
questions.explanation: In suspected Placenta Previa, digital vaginal examination is strictly contraindicated because fingers can tear placental tissue and cause life-threatening torrential hemorrhage.
subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
Radiology

questions.question: During surgery in the carotid triangle, direct mechanical stimulation of the carotid sinus nerve (nerve of Hering) triggers reflex bradycardia and hypotension. The afferent limb of this baroreceptor reflex is carried by which cranial nerve?
questions.explanation: The carotid sinus baroreceptor afferents travel via the sinus nerve of Hering to the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX), whereas aortic arch baroreceptor afferents travel via the vagus nerve (CN X).
subject: Physiology
Anatomy

questions.question: A 40-year-old psychiatric patient on Haloperidol presents with acute severe fever (40.2°C), generalized 'lead-pipe' muscle rigidity, autonomic instability, and markedly elevated serum creatine kinase. What is the first-line pharmacotherapeutic agent?
questions.explanation: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) is managed by immediate discontinuation of antipsychotics, supportive cooling, and administration of Dantrolene (RYR1 blocker) or Bromocriptine (dopamine agonist).
subject: Psychiatry
Pharmacology

questions.question: Which histological feature on liver biopsy is pathognomonic of alcoholic hepatitis?
options: Mallory-Denk bodies (damaged cytokeratin filaments) and neutrophilic infiltration
Non-caseating epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells
questions.explanation: Alcoholic hepatitis is characterized histologically by hepatocyte ballooning, neutrophilic inflammation, pericellular sinusoidal fibrosis, and eosinophilic intracytoplasmic Mallory-Denk bodies.
subject: Pathology

questions.question: A 6-year-old child presents with colicky abdominal pain, palpable purpuric lesions over the buttocks and lower extremities, and hematuria following an upper respiratory infection. Platelet count is normal. What is the underlying immunopathogenesis?
options: IgA immune complex deposition in small vessel walls (Henoch-Schönlein purpura)
Anti-platelet GP IIb/IIIa autoantibody mediated destruction
Necrotizing transmural vasculitis of medium arteries
questions.explanation: IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schönlein purpura) is a systemic leukocytoclastic small-vessel vasculitis caused by tissue deposition of IgA-containing immune complexes in the skin, GI tract, joints, and renal mesangium.
subject: Pediatrics
Dermatology
General Medicine

questions.question: A 23-year-old male with untreated Chronic Suppurative Otitis Media (CSOM) presents with high-spiking 'picket-fence' fevers, chills, and tenderness along the sternocleidomastoid muscle (Griesinger's sign). What intracranial venous structure is thrombosed?
options: Sigmoid (lateral) sinus and internal jugular vein
questions.explanation: Lateral/sigmoid sinus thrombophlebitis secondary to mastoiditis presents with 'picket-fence' septic spikes, torticollis, and mastoid emissary vein thrombosis (Griesinger sign).
subject: ENT
General Surgery

questions.question: A pure-tone audiogram reveals a bilateral symmetrical sensorineural dip maximal at 4000 Hz with normal speech discrimination in quiet surroundings. This pattern is characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Noise-induced hearing loss characteristically manifests as an acoustic dip or notch in bone and air conduction at 4000 Hz, with partial recovery at 8000 Hz.
subject: ENT
PSM / Community Med

questions.question: What is the sensory dermatomal block level required for performing a lower segment Cesarean section under spinal subarachnoid anesthesia without peritoneal discomfort?
questions.explanation: Spinal anesthesia for Cesarean delivery requires a sensory dermatomal block up to T4 to prevent pain and visceral nausea during peritoneal traction and exteriorization of the uterus.
subject: Anesthesia
Obstetrics & Gynaecology

questions.question: An emergency contrast CT scan in an elderly patient with sudden-onset tearing interscapular back pain and unequal radial pulses demonstrates an intimal flap originating distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. According to the Stanford classification, what is this lesion and its initial management?
options: Stanford Type B Aortic Dissection; initial medical management with IV Esmolol / Labetalol
Stanford Type A Aortic Dissection; immediate emergency open surgical replacement
DeBakey Type I Dissection; urgent pericardiocentesis
Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm rupture; emergent exploratory laparotomy
questions.explanation: Stanford Type B involves only the descending aorta distal to the left subclavian artery. Uncomplicated Type B dissections are managed medically with IV beta-blockers to lower HR and shear stress (<120 mmHg systolic).
subject: Radiology
General Surgery
General Medicine

questions.question: A 45-year-old woman with a palpable anterior neck nodule undergoes FNAC. Smears reveal overlapping enlarged ground-glass nuclei ('Orphan Annie eye'), longitudinal nuclear grooves, and psammoma bodies. What is the definitive diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Papillary thyroid carcinoma is recognized by optically clear nuclei ('Orphan Annie'), nuclear pseudoinclusions/grooves, and concentric calcified psammoma bodies.
subject: Pathology
General Surgery

questions.question: During evaluation of a 62-year-old male with obstructive voiding symptoms, digital rectal examination reveals an asymmetrically enlarged, rock-hard, non-tender nodule in the prostate peripheral zone. Serum PSA is 18 ng/mL. Which zone of the prostate is the most common site of origin for adenocarcinoma?
questions.explanation: Approximately 70-75% of prostate carcinomas originate in the peripheral zone (accessible on DRE), whereas benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) arises from the transition zone.
subject: General Surgery
Pathology

questions.question: A 24-year-old primigravida at 38 weeks presents in active labor. Cardiotocography reveals recurrent late decelerations that mirror uterine contractions with delayed nadir. What is the pathophysiological significance of this tracing?
options: Benign fetal head compression causing vagal response
questions.explanation: Late decelerations are characterized by a nadir occurring after the peak of uterine contractions, indicating decreased intervillous blood flow, uteroplacental insufficiency, and impending fetal metabolic acidosis.
subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
Physiology
